dailyGuidance.title: Begin within Hukam
dailyGuidance.summary: The day does not need to come under your control before it can be met truthfully.

dailyGuidance.title: Win the inner field first
dailyGuidance.summary: Guru does not tell you to dominate others. Guru tells you where the real contest lives.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not waste the crossing
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the day that stays busy but spiritually unspent. The line turns life from ornament into crossing, and asks for effort while the chance is still open.

dailyGuidance.title: Stay where the heart is helped
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the soul being shaped by whatever company it keeps. The line says life becomes meeting and remembrance in holy company, not in private drift.

dailyGuidance.title: Let service stay hidden and real
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the good work that has started asking to be noticed. The line says service stays true when the self is no longer its hidden audience.

dailyGuidance.title: Keep command and Naam in one breath
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the split between outward obedience and inward resistance. The line keeps the two together: obey the Guru's command with the whole mind, and keep the Name alive inside the heart.

dailyGuidance.title: Ask who is speaking when ego sounds ordinary
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when ego wears the plain clothes of common sense. The line breaks that spell by refusing to call the voice natural or final.

dailyGuidance.title: Let pain uncover what comfort was hiding
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when suffering feels useless and only punishing. The line says pain can uncover the dependence that easy days keep hidden.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop arguing with what already stands
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that wants reality to arrive on self-approved terms. The line places doing back in the Creator's hands and quiets the argument that you were meant to run the day.

dailyGuidance.title: Stand inside the care already holding you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the body leaning toward the worst outcome. The line answers fear with the Creator's mercy and protection, steadier than your wavering.

dailyGuidance.title: Receive before demanding more
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart that notices absence faster than gift. The line says gratitude becomes honest when mercy is named before complaint.

dailyGuidance.title: Receive the nearness you keep overlooking
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets loneliness when it has started narrating abandonment. The line says longing ripens in holy company and the soul is led like a cherished child, not left to wander alone.

dailyGuidance.title: Let remembrance outrun the spiral
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets anxiety before it settles fully into the body. The line sends remembrance into breath, chest, and thought until worry loses its right to rule.

dailyGuidance.title: Earn cleanly and keep the hand open
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets work that has become costume, accumulation, or self-display. The line honors the one who earns honestly, shares freely, and lets labor stay clean.

dailyGuidance.title: Let praise and insult lose their claim
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when other people's words still set the temperature inside you. The line names freedom as sameness under praise and slander, not only detachment from possessions.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not insult the doorway through which you came
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets contempt while it is still pretending to be casual speech. The line strips off that disguise by naming woman as the doorway through which life itself arrives.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop arguing with what already stands
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that wants reality on self-approved terms. The line teaches a harder peace: receive under the Lord's pleasure rather than keep litigating the day.

dailyGuidance.title: You cannot clutch what mercy has to give
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the grasping heart that wants Naam as one more possession. The line says the jewel is given by mercy, while the self-willed hand loses what it tries to hold.

dailyGuidance.title: All are already within the River of Life
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the reflex to divide life into inside and outside, mine and not mine. The line answers with something larger: the One is the River of Life, there is no second, and every being is already within Him.

dailyGuidance.title: Speak only what can stand at the Door
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mouth that still wants the sharp sentence because it feels strong. The line measures speech by whether it can stand at the Lord's Door with honor.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not give your mouth to the wound
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the hot second before speech goes looking for damage. The line says the tongue needs a master stronger than hurt: truth, praise, and restraint.

dailyGuidance.title: Make room for the Name by wanting less
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a life so crowded by appetite that the inner room stays noisy. The line asks what kind of gain still leaves space for Naam to live inside the heart.

dailyGuidance.title: Wandering will not quench this fire
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the restless search for clarity through more movement, more content, and more distance. The line says doubt is not burned out by travel but by the Guru's word within.

dailyGuidance.title: Return before reopening every question
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps reopening what was already clear enough to obey. The line says doubt clears when the Guru's word is kept longer than the wandering mood.

dailyGuidance.title: Go where selfishness can soften
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the day when private effort has turned stale and self-absorbed. The line says peace returns by joining true company, dropping selfishness, and letting the heart be carried with others.

dailyGuidance.title: Trade for what crosses the last threshold
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the day spent polishing what death cannot carry. The line asks for profit the soul can still recognize at departure.

dailyGuidance.title: A deal can fatten the hand and empty the soul
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the bargain that looks profitable while leaving the heart thinner. The line asks what kind of gain will still know your name at the final crossing.

dailyGuidance.title: Spend this day on profit that remains
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a day swollen with tasks and thin in meaning. The line says human life is a chance to meet, serve, and earn what actually remains.

dailyGuidance.title: Give the tongue a truer master
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the split between devout speech and ordinary conduct. The line says remembrance is real only when it sweetens the mouth and lowers the walk.

dailyGuidance.title: Return before reopening every question
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps reopening what was already clear enough to obey. The line cuts doubt from the inside by returning you to lived remembrance.

dailyGuidance.title: Keep one repetition until it changes you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets devotion that keeps restarting because it never stays with one repetition long enough to become habit. The line says steadiness is born from one clean return practiced past mood.

dailyGuidance.title: Choose settlement over motion
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the search that keeps accelerating while clarity does not. The line says searching ripens only when it comes near shelter and holy company.

dailyGuidance.title: Mercy cools the body into patience
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the overheated mind after mercy has finally arrived. The line says patience is not forced; it is what settles when holy company cools mind and body and the Lord comes near within.

dailyGuidance.title: Fast from retaliation
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the wound at the moment it wants another sentence, another defense, another moral advantage. The line calls forgiveness the real fast because it changes conduct before it changes feelings.

dailyGuidance.title: Let reverence replace the room fear built
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart that has grown used to living under threat. The line says fear loosens where reverence, right conduct, and contentment begin to govern instead.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the heart open under one clear word
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the closed inner life that keeps mistaking analysis for opening. The line says the heart opens where one clear word is kept long enough to bloom.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the search end in company, not novelty
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a hunger that is sincere but keeps scattering itself across new voices and new roads. The line says wandering ends where guidance, company, and devotion finally become home.

dailyGuidance.title: Let waiting ripen into listening
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets delay when it has already started souring into resentment. The line asks patience to listen longer than it complains so honor can return to the wait.

dailyGuidance.title: Trade in Naam, not passing profit
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the appetite for gain that still leaves the heart poor. The line says true wealth is earned in Naam, and patience lets that trade ripen into honor.

dailyGuidance.title: Pure conduct outranks spiritual display.
dailyGuidance.summary: Guru does not leave the religious life undefined. The better religion is the one that purifies action, not the one that performs itself most loudly.

dailyGuidance.title: Give the tongue a truer master
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mouth that wants to sound spiritual without becoming clean. The line says the truest religion is conduct sustained by Naam, not speech performing devotion.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the life match the line
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the gap between devotional language and actual conduct. The line says the heart becomes holy only when the life beneath it turns clean.

dailyGuidance.title: Held close in the hidden hour
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the hour when distance feels more believable than care. The line answers by naming a closeness the Lord Himself keeps.

dailyGuidance.title: Stand where you are cherished
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the ache to earn tenderness through achievement. The line does something simpler: it calls God father and mother and lets the soul stand there as a cherished child.

dailyGuidance.title: Nearness is worth more than what desire begs for
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the scramble for wealth, notice, and the kind of desire that turns the self into a beggar. The line says the Lord holds the humble servant near, and that nearness outranks what craving asks from the room.

dailyGuidance.title: Let forgiveness widen the whole room
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when peace returns to you but has not yet been trusted with anyone else. The line says forgiveness should spread peace outward, not end in private relief.

dailyGuidance.title: Keep peace alive with Bani
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment after relief, when silence could either deepen into devotion or drift back into noise. The line says lasting peace has to be sung, kept, and fed by Bani.

dailyGuidance.title: Let grace settle what you cannot
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the part of life you keep trying to force into resolution. The line says grace settles what strain cannot, and peace grows where the heart stops insisting on control.

dailyGuidance.title: Nothing stands outside Hukam
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind still treating some outcomes as exceptions. The line says body, status, pain, blessing, and wandering all unfold within Hukam.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop arguing with what already stands
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that still wants exceptions to Hukam. The line says everything stands within that order, and ego thins when this is actually seen.

dailyGuidance.title: Put discipline on the body
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the wish to look serious without being changed. The line remakes discipline as contentment, humility, and meditation worn plainly.

dailyGuidance.title: Let contentment prove your discipline
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the wish to look disciplined while the mind still runs loose. The line makes contentment, humility, and Naam the real mark.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not waste a body built for meeting
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a life in danger of being spent entirely on upkeep. The line begins with the body as gift, which means it already carries responsibility.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not spend a rare life like loose change
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a day filling up while the reason for being alive grows faint. The line says human life is rare meeting ground, not something to spend by drift.

dailyGuidance.title: Serve without making yourself the headline
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the part of service still wanting witness, credit, or moral glow. The line is sharp: clean service does not advertise itself.

dailyGuidance.title: Do the work without pricing it
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the inner ledger still counting recognition and return. The line says selfless service dies when reward becomes part of the motive.

dailyGuidance.title: Serve without auditioning for reward
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the subtle bargain hiding inside good work. The line says service becomes true when reward is not the secret reason.

dailyGuidance.title: Start where ego is finally questioned
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the defensive moment that still assumes the self is right. The line becomes medicine by asking where ego comes from and how it can actually leave.

dailyGuidance.title: Take the cure, not the diagnosis
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when recognizing ego starts becoming one more intelligent pose. The line insists that naming the sickness is not enough; the medicine has to be taken.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not call the fever your personality
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self getting mistaken for instinct, honesty, or force of character. The line says ego is a fever, and the Guru's medicine has to be taken before it starts feeling natural.

dailyGuidance.title: Let pain teach what comfort keeps hiding
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the instinct to call pleasure blessing and pain failure. The line reverses that instinct by saying suffering can reopen desire for God.

dailyGuidance.title: Let helplessness tell the truth
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when suffering strips away self-sufficiency. The line makes pain medicinal when it drives you out of illusion.

dailyGuidance.title: Let praise carry what effort cannot
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the point where strain has already proved insufficient. The line turns the heart from effort to praise as a real crossing.

dailyGuidance.title: Let mercy stop the wavering
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the shaky moment when provision feels uncertain and the mind starts swaying. The line answers with the Creator's mercy and ongoing care.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop wavering where mercy already holds you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the body leaning toward the worst outcome. The line answers wavering with the Creator's mercy and protection.

dailyGuidance.title: Let gratitude become honest again
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the ashamed heart that knows it has received more than it has recognized. The line turns unworthiness into thankful dependence and a plea for Naam.

dailyGuidance.title: Mercy restores the gratitude you ignored
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart living on mercy it barely notices. The line joins confession and gratitude so the gift can be felt again.

dailyGuidance.title: Ask to be shown the way
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the lonely ache that does not know how to reach the Beloved on its own. The line turns longing toward saint-company instead of private brooding.

dailyGuidance.title: Ask the path inside holy company
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the lonely ache that keeps asking in private circles. The line says the way becomes clearer where the Beloved already dwells: among the true congregation.

dailyGuidance.title: Let yourself be kept like a child
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when the heart has no sturdy voice left. The line lets helplessness become trust by receiving the Guru as mother and father.

dailyGuidance.title: Remember until the mind stops sprinting
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets an anxious mind already running ahead of the body. The line is simple on purpose: remembrance is the way back to peace.

dailyGuidance.title: Let simran cool the body from within
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets anxiety after it has already entered the jaw, chest, or stomach. The line says remembrance is not decorative sound; it is meant to cool the body from the inside.

dailyGuidance.title: Honor the one through whom you arrived
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the casual contempt that speaks lightly of women while depending on them for everything. The line breaks that contempt by tracing life, love, and kingship through woman.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not insult the source of life
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets speech or culture that belittles women while depending on them. The line is a public rebuke of contempt.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not bow to performative holiness
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets religious display emptied of labor, wisdom, and generosity. The line refuses fake authority and honors the one who works and gives.

dailyGuidance.title: Honest work makes the path visible
dailyGuidance.summary: Seva becomes credible in honest labor and open-handed giving, not in spiritual performance.

dailyGuidance.title: Earn honestly and let some leave your hand
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the split between livelihood and devotion. The line refuses the split: honest work and sharing are part of the path itself.

dailyGuidance.title: Rest where attachment cannot rule
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the tired heart that keeps gripping people, outcomes, and opinion for stability. The line places rest in the Lord's shelter, not in possession.

dailyGuidance.title: Hold the gift without gripping it
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind clinging to what it cannot finally keep. The line says steadiness grows where attachment loses its authority and the gift is received without possession.

dailyGuidance.title: Receive what is given under Hukam
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the struggle with outcomes you did not choose. The line places giving and receiving back under the Lord's will.

dailyGuidance.title: Receive what is given and keep the Naam
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that receives with resentment. The line joins receiving to the Lord's pleasure and mercy to the Jewel of Naam.

dailyGuidance.title: Receive reunion without forgetting the Doer
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart that wants to claim return as its own achievement. The line teaches reunion under the Lord's pleasure because the Creator is still the Doer.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not let the mouth become a dumping ground
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets speech already fouled by greed, slander, anger, and self-praise. The line insists that only words bringing honor are worth keeping.

dailyGuidance.title: Choose the word that can bear honor
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a mouth ready to wound, posture, or bargain. The line asks for words that can survive truth.

dailyGuidance.title: Roaming will not put doubt out
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the hope that a new setting or method will finally quiet the mind. The line says doubt travels well.

dailyGuidance.title: Wandering will not cool this fire
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps moving because stillness feels risky. The line says doubt is not cured by distance, only by becoming Gurmukh.

dailyGuidance.title: Drop the private case
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that wants peace without giving up its self-importance. The line says doubt clears when selfishness loosens inside true company.

dailyGuidance.title: Buy what can follow you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the ache to secure yourself by gathering more. The line asks a cleaner question: what can still follow you when the deal, the object, and the image are gone?

dailyGuidance.title: Carry praise, not counterfeit profit
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the buyer's instinct to secure the self with goods that cannot stay. The line says take the merchandise of praise, the only wealth that survives the crossing.

dailyGuidance.title: Let Naam thin the inner dread
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind still carrying weight after the deal is done. The line says true profit is the fearlessness that grows when Naam lives within.

dailyGuidance.title: Let peace reach the mouth and the walk
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets devotional effort that still feels theatrical and restless. The line says peace grows in saintly company until speech sweetens and the walk humbles.

dailyGuidance.title: Sweet speech is a path, not polish
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the temptation to make speech beautiful while the life stays proud. The line joins sweetness, humility, peace, and union in one path.

dailyGuidance.title: Let searching speak its real hunger
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the restless heart that keeps moving without naming what it wants. The line admits the search plainly so it can be brought where it finally cools.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop roaming for what saintly company gives
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the exhausted spiritual search that keeps mistaking motion for nearness. The line says techniques and travel cannot make peace arrive; saintly company can.

dailyGuidance.title: Let holy company cool the body
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets restlessness that has already become physical heat. The line says saintly company cools mind and body together.

dailyGuidance.title: Practice forgiveness until fear loosens
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets resentment disguised as strength. The line makes forgiveness a discipline of conduct and contentment, not a soft feeling.

dailyGuidance.title: Practice forgiveness until fear loses its stage
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the guarded heart that calls its tension caution. The line ties forgiveness, conduct, and contentment together until fear shrinks.

dailyGuidance.title: Let saintly company end the mind's pacing
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets impatience as mental wandering. The line says composure grows by dwelling among those who already carry it.

dailyGuidance.title: Let patience gather real wealth
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the wandering mind that wants quick proof and visible gain. The line says true wealth is Naam, and patience ripens into honor in holy company.

dailyGuidance.title: Let religion show up in conduct
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the habit of praising religion in words while excusing behavior. The line pushes the question down into life.

dailyGuidance.title: Let devotion show up in conduct
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the split between devotional language and lived behavior. The line refuses that split by calling religion true only when Naam and conduct stay together.

dailyGuidance.title: Let your worth come from being held
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the insecure heart that keeps begging the world to confirm it. The line says true worth begins when the Guru enshrines the Lord within.

dailyGuidance.title: Measure greatness by what the heart holds
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self still looking for worth in scale or applause. The line says the greatest keep the Lord clasped in the heart.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not waste the peace forgiveness brings
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the quiet after pardon, when peace has returned but devotion has not yet answered it. The line treats forgiveness as the beginning of worship, not the end of crisis.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop feeding the rehearsed wound
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the wound after it has already become a daily rehearsal. The line says lasting peace arrives when forgiveness ripens into return, not when replay gets one more turn.

dailyGuidance.title: Turn received peace into praise
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment after relief, when the heart is tempted to drift back into old noise. The line says lasting peace stays living by Bani and Naam, not by memory alone.

dailyGuidance.title: Truth was here before your urgency
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the tightened moment when everything feels like it depends on your grip. The line breaks that spell by naming a truth older than your fear.

dailyGuidance.title: Piling up will not satisfy hunger
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the appetite that keeps promising one more acquisition will settle everything. The line exposes a hunger that grows faster than whatever you stack in front of it.

dailyGuidance.title: Cleverness cannot walk beside you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind still bargaining for control through strategy and brilliance. The line strips that illusion and leaves one durable path: walk in Hukam.

dailyGuidance.title: Let praise loosen your need to grasp
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that wants reality explained, managed, and pinned down. The line opens the field wider: people sing of His power, but no one contains it.

dailyGuidance.title: Let vastness loosen your grip
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that wants to manage what is far larger than itself. The line opens a different posture: the One is already watching, already present, already beyond your control.

dailyGuidance.title: Ask holy company to hold you close
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart that keeps trying to carry longing privately. The line asks for closeness from companions who can hold devotion with you.

dailyGuidance.title: Learn love from those who live it
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the seeker who wants closeness without company. The line sends you into the embrace of companions who already know how to love the Lord.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the scheme die before it runs you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the proud mind that keeps trying to save itself with plans. The line says rescue begins when ego is subdued and useless scheming is dropped.

dailyGuidance.title: Meet the True One before you brace
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that answers fear with more control. The line says fear departs when the True One is met and ego softens.

dailyGuidance.title: Melt the self into praise
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind hardened by self-consciousness and comparison. The line imagines praise as fusion, not performance.

dailyGuidance.title: Let praise dye the whole life true
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self-consciousness comparison keeps hardening. The line says praise and saintly company should dye the whole life truthful.

dailyGuidance.title: True action finds the inward door
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self-conscious life that admires truth without embodying it. The line says this body is given for true action, and the way home is found within.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not decorate the life that forgot the Beloved
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the life still polished on the outside while divided within. The line says without the Shabad and the Husband Lord, every decoration stays false.

dailyGuidance.title: Without the Beloved, decoration stays hollow
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the effort to look radiant while the heart is estranged. The line asks what ornaments can do when duality has already left the bride abandoned.

dailyGuidance.title: No shelter holds the false self
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets loneliness still trying to hide in false shelters. The line says what is false will not protect you here or hereafter.

dailyGuidance.title: Ask the Guru before you scatter
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the anxious search for the right practice, teacher, or move. The line steadies the question by turning it toward the Guru instead of frantic self-invention.

dailyGuidance.title: Stay awake over what the Guru has given
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the inattentive mind that asks for guidance and then drifts. The line says asking the Guru is not enough; you must stay awake enough to guard the field.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop waiting for the right time
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the delaying mind that honors practice in theory and postpones it in life. The line asks a sharp question: if not now, when does remembrance begin?

dailyGuidance.title: Stop waiting for a better time
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the delaying mind that keeps planning devotion for later. The line strips away the excuse: the true time is now, night and day.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Shabad clear the double mind
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the fog that keeps reopening what was already shown. The line says the Guru's word fills the heart with reverence and cleans the dirt of duality.

dailyGuidance.title: Without the Beloved, even one instant burns
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps dressing longing up as uncertainty. The line says the Shabad fills the heart with reverent awe, and without the Beloved even one instant burns.

dailyGuidance.title: Cherish the Lord by relying on mercy
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the soul that still wants closeness without dependence. The line makes love sound childlike again: it rests on mercy first.

dailyGuidance.title: Be a child honest about your mistakes
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the ashamed heart that wants mercy without honesty. The line brings both together: love the Lord, admit the mistake, and stay under the care of Father and Mother.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop arguing with what already stands
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind resisting what has happened because failure feels unbearable. The line says peace begins when truth about the loss is brought into mercy instead of argument.

dailyGuidance.title: Go where death loses its swagger
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the inflamed self that keeps fighting alone. The line says humble company breaks the fear hiding underneath the heat.

dailyGuidance.title: Fear recedes in humble company
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the alarmed state that tries to survive by closing in on itself. The line says safety grows where the humble gather and the Merciful One settles in the mind.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Court decide what honor is
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the ache to be seen, thanked, and called worthy now. The line turns the heart away from the room and toward the Court, where love-filled service is what receives honor.

dailyGuidance.title: Gather love at the Guru's feet
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart scattered across too many loves at once. The line gathers mind and body back to the Guru's feet.

dailyGuidance.title: Let holy company lift Maya's dust
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets attachment after it has already settled into the heart. The line says two things clear it: love for the Guru with mind and body, and life inside holy company.

dailyGuidance.title: Let seeking kneel before it wanders
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the search that keeps multiplying methods while resisting surrender. The line sends the search to Naam and the Guru's service.

dailyGuidance.title: Let seeking become service
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the hunger that keeps searching without landing. The line says release is not found by roaming, but by the True Name and service to the True Guru.

dailyGuidance.title: Let fresh Naam settle inside
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the tired wandering mind that keeps looking for novelty outside itself. The line says the freshest thing is Naam abiding within.

dailyGuidance.title: Choose settlement over motion
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when movement is increasing but clarity is not. The line says stay still long enough for fresh Naam to settle before motion takes over again.

dailyGuidance.title: Serve until mind and body agree
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the split between spiritual speech and ordinary conduct. The line says serving the True Guru makes the mind immaculate and the body pure together.

dailyGuidance.title: Let service make room for the Lord
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the useful act that still carries a trace of self-display. The line says serving the True Guru lets the Lord dwell in the mind and keeps filth from clinging.

dailyGuidance.title: Peace comes by serving, not starring
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self that wants inner light without obedience. The line joins peace to serving the True Guru and recognizing the self honestly.

dailyGuidance.title: Let praise become the place you live
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self that still wants peace while staying at the center. The line says peace grows by serving the Guru and dwelling in the praise carried by the Shabad.

dailyGuidance.title: Ask to be kept by the Will
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when self-direction is failing but pride still resists surrender. The line becomes relief by asking to be kept according to the Beloved's pleasure.

dailyGuidance.title: Belonging is not a private possession
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self that keeps guarding worth like scarce property. The line widens the heart by saying all belong to the One, and the One belongs to all.

dailyGuidance.title: Receive the belonging you did not manufacture
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self that keeps trying to secure belonging through position or force. The line says belonging is received from the One who already holds everyone.

dailyGuidance.title: Learning is empty when Maya is still loved
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the person who keeps collecting religious words while staying attached to the same old cravings. The line exposes knowledge without inward turning.

dailyGuidance.title: Recognize the One within before you teach
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the religious or intellectual mood that can explain everything except the heart. The line says loud learning is empty if the Divine is still unrecognized within.

dailyGuidance.title: Serve until the complaint quiets
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the restless habit of thinking harder while avoiding the next faithful act. The line says service ripens into Naam, and the inner noise begins to fall.

dailyGuidance.title: Let complaint leave the mouth
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that has grown used to crying out, muttering, and protesting. The line says service ripens into a quieter heart where complaint no longer rules the tongue.

dailyGuidance.title: Let service make your life weighty
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the dull feeling that nothing you do is reaching beyond maintenance. The line says service to the Lord is fruitful and honors the one who lives from it.

dailyGuidance.title: Let service become the way across
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the useful life that is still spiritually unplaced. The line says service is not merely good activity; through the Shabad it becomes a path across.

dailyGuidance.title: Stubbornness is not a spiritual path
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the seeker who keeps trying to force arrival through self-will. The line refuses that posture and says true service begins where the Lord Himself draws you near.

dailyGuidance.title: The brave fight is inward
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self that still wants victory over other people. The line redefines courage as subduing the vicious ego within.

dailyGuidance.title: Be brave enough to kill the inner tyrant
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the urge to look brave while arrogance still runs the house. The line says the real warrior subdues inner ego and redeems life through praise.

dailyGuidance.title: Call courage what happens after ego kneels
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self that still mistakes dominance for strength. The line says courage begins where ego kneels, not where it swells.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Name clear the fog
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the inner confusion that keeps reopening what was already shown. The line says the Guru plants Naam so doubt loses its house and the path brightens.

dailyGuidance.title: Sing until doubt loses its room
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the foggy mind that wants clarity without devotion. The line says doubt thins when Naam is implanted deeply enough to be sung.

dailyGuidance.title: Make the hands good by what they serve
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the ordinary use of hands that leaves no trace of praise. The line says hands become good when they help the Lord's praise take form.

dailyGuidance.title: Use your hands for praise, not stain
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a body acting all day without much of it turning upward. The line blesses hands used for praise and clean work.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Bani cool what is burning
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the overheated heart that has had enough of its own inner weather. The line says the Lord's Bani is not decoration but nectar.

dailyGuidance.title: Hear the Bani until it lifts you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the impatient habit of tasting Bani once and moving on. The line says ascent comes through repeated hearing, not novelty.

dailyGuidance.title: Let shelter be personal again
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets fear when it has made the world feel parentless and exposed. The line answers with startling nearness: Father, Mother, kin, protector.

dailyGuidance.title: Let protection become felt, not recited
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets fear that still talks about God from a distance. The line makes protection intimate: Father, Mother, and shelter everywhere.

dailyGuidance.title: The battlefield changes when the Guru is with you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the frightened feeling that life has become one long contest. The line says victory comes through the Perfect Guru, not through panic's private weapons.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the mind lean where life comes from
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the worn heart that keeps trying to support itself alone. The line places life and mental support back in the One who already carries them.

dailyGuidance.title: Rest the mind on what already carries it
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the overextended mind still trying to hold itself up. The line says peace comes when the heart rests on the One who is already its breath and support.

dailyGuidance.title: Mercy brings the Name home
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the seeker who cannot force inward arrival. The line says even the disciplined and gifted still wait on mercy for the Name to enter the home of the mind.

dailyGuidance.title: Let worth be received in truth
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the fragile self that borrows dignity from reaction and approval. The line says those attuned to Truth are absorbed into what is most real, not into what others say.

dailyGuidance.title: Let Truth give your heart its place
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the fragile craving to be confirmed by response, praise, or position. The line says worth becomes steadier when the Shabad shows the One within and Truth becomes the measure.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop measuring inside a filled world
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets comparison when scarcity has entered the eyes. The line interrupts it by naming the Divine already pervading every color and form.

dailyGuidance.title: Scarcity breaks when the world is already full
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the comparing gaze that keeps turning abundance into rivalry. The line says the One is already pervading every form, while comparison only keeps the cycle turning.

dailyGuidance.title: Serve until separation starts healing
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the ache of long separation and devotional dryness. The line says day-and-night service and remembrance begin healing what lifetimes of distance have done.

dailyGuidance.title: Give longing to service, not performance
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets separation before it turns into self-display. The line keeps the ache in service and remembrance because no other comfort holds.

dailyGuidance.title: Enter the teaching as given
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that wants even the path on its own terms. The heading itself slows you down: entry into the teaching is received, not improvised.

dailyGuidance.title: Begin under the Name before anything else
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the tired mind that wants relief before orientation. The opening places everything under the One, Truth, and the Guru's grace before any other claim is allowed to speak.

dailyGuidance.title: Trust the cooling house
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets weariness that keeps spending trust in the wrong places. The line says the Guru is cooling shelter and lasting wealth, and peace follows when the mind rests there.

dailyGuidance.title: Notice how appetite grows
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the excuse that craving is harmless because it feels natural. The line begins at the first attachment and starts tracing how appetite learns to rule.

dailyGuidance.title: Watch appetite grow before it rules you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets desire before it has fully named itself as need. The line traces how appetite grows by stages until it begins ruling the life.

dailyGuidance.title: When the soul asks the way, do not walk alone
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the late realization that appetite has not taught the way home. The line says the soul must ask direction, because the world without the Guru is already drowning.

dailyGuidance.title: Bring regret under mercy, not despair
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind stuck staring at what cannot be undone. The line does not deny consequence, but it places karma beneath the larger mercy and Name of God.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop arguing with what is already under Hukam
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps replaying what should have happened differently. The line says what pleases the Divine comes to pass, whether your argument is ready or not.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the deeper fear swallow the lesser ones
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart scattered by a hundred small fears. The line says the one who tastes Naam forgets the lesser fears that used to organize the day.

dailyGuidance.title: Let Naam swallow the smaller fears
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets a mind crowded by lesser alarms. The line says those absorbed in Naam forget the secondary fears instead of negotiating with each one.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the filled heart leave doubt behind
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps reopening uncertainty. The line says wholeness comes when the heart is filled with the Lord day and night, and doubt falls away there.

dailyGuidance.title: Let wandering end where the Guru leads
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets spiritual restlessness that keeps circling visible forms and ideas. The line says the deeper union is known only through the True Guru.

dailyGuidance.title: Service carries the seeker across
dailyGuidance.summary: Restlessness eases when devotion and service stop being abstractions and become the next faithful act.

dailyGuidance.title: Let devotion quiet the wandering appetite
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps hoping more variety will finally satisfy it. The line says bliss comes through devotion, until the heart rests at the Lord's feet.

dailyGuidance.title: A passing drama is too short for waste
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the restless mood that treats the body like permanent shelter and the day like endless inventory. The line brings mortality close enough to clean up urgency.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not spend the passing day in gossip
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets restless speech that keeps burning through a life already brief. The line places passing-world clarity beside lies, slander, and gossip.

dailyGuidance.title: Give the frantic mind a mantra
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind scattering itself in ten directions at once. The line says the Perfect Guru quiets that roaming by placing the Lord's mantra at the center.

dailyGuidance.title: Restless hearts also need love
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps moving because it has forgotten what it is moving toward. The line joins aimless wandering to a heart missing love for the Lord.

dailyGuidance.title: Take the crowded body into saintly company
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the body-village already crowded by sexual desire and anger. The line says those forces were broken to pieces when the Holy Saint was finally met.

dailyGuidance.title: Your turning was written as grace
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the urge to treat your spiritual turning as self-made. The line says two things together: the old heat was broken by holy company, and meeting the Guru came by pre-ordained grace.

dailyGuidance.title: Turn back before distance hardens into pain
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the stubborn drift that keeps making pain bite deeper. The line warns that distance worsens the wound, then turns back to Naam as support.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not mistake nearness for taste
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the soul living close to the treasure but still unable to taste it. The line says mercy is what turns nearness into sweetness.

dailyGuidance.title: Mercy lets the hidden sweetness be found
dailyGuidance.summary: Mercy is not forced out of the day. The heart tastes what was already near when the Merciful One opens it.

dailyGuidance.title: Grace reaches first
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart that keeps assuming kindness must first be earned. The line says grace is what turns nearness into something tasted rather than merely talked about.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the body learn surrender first
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self that admires devotion while still bargaining with it. The line is physical and uncompromising: the body itself is given to the Guru.

dailyGuidance.title: Give yourself where love can be trained
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self still trying to belong without surrender. The line says love deepens when body, fear, and doubt are handed to the Guru.

dailyGuidance.title: Accept what the Beloved sends
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when the heart starts resisting what has already been given. The line turns complaint into consent before bitterness hardens.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Beloved's way please you
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when the heart keeps arguing with what has already arrived. The line turns acceptance into affection instead of grim resignation.

dailyGuidance.title: Let service steady your honor
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the protest that keeps asking the room to confirm your worth. The line lets the Beloved's way grow dearer than wounded pride.

dailyGuidance.title: Put your hope where the world cannot reach
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the body that keeps bracing for the next blow, opinion, or reversal. The line says the world's reach weakens when hope is placed in the Lord.

dailyGuidance.title: Fill the heart until fear finds no place
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the nervous system that keeps scanning for threat. The line says safety comes from a heart occupied by the Lord.

dailyGuidance.title: Let hope outrank the world's reach
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the hour when visible power starts feeling more real than divine care. The line says hope in the Lord shrinks what the world can actually threaten.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not waste the rare chance of a human life
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the sleepy assumption that there will always be more time. The line treats human birth as rare fortune, not a casual repeatable resource.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not spend this rare life asleep
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the life being spent in appetite, distraction, and delay. The line reminds you the human body was obtained with difficulty and can still be wasted.

dailyGuidance.title: Ownership fails at the first question
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the possessive cry of mine. The line uses simple questions to expose how quickly ownership collapses.

dailyGuidance.title: Do not let grief turn into ownership
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the panicked noise that rises when the mind treats people as possessions. The line breaks that spell by naming kinship as temporary and arrival as Hukam.

dailyGuidance.title: Seeming great is not being great
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the reflex to feel small beside visible power. The line interrupts that spell by stressing appearance before worth.

dailyGuidance.title: Measure greatness by what the heart clings to
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the envy that mistakes public size for true worth. The line says greatness belongs to the one whose attachment is fastened to the Lord.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the heart be kept in what is complete
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the chronic sense that something essential is missing. The line says the path, cleansing, peace, and honor become whole when Naam lives in the heart.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Perfect One keep your standing
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the fear of losing face. The line moves honor out of public management and into the keeping of the Perfect Lord.

dailyGuidance.title: Leave their portion and keep your own heart
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that keeps watching another life instead of tending its own. The line returns wholeness to the heart that keeps Naam rather than score.

dailyGuidance.title: Go where the heart is washed clean
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the grimy inner feeling left by envy, ego, and self-measuring. The line says holy company cleans more deeply than private polishing ever can.

dailyGuidance.title: Go where ego comes off
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self trying to cleanse itself without surrender. The line says ego actually falls in saintly company.

dailyGuidance.title: Take comparison to the washing place
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets comparison after it has already dirtied the heart. The line says clean company and Naam are stronger than the measuring habit.

dailyGuidance.title: Ask for the saint who can show the way
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets bewilderment that has finally run out of private strategies. The line turns the cry itself into wisdom: ask for the saint who can give peace and show the way.

dailyGuidance.title: Take your doubt to saintly company
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind worn out by questions. The line admits the world is asleep in attachment and asks for living guidance.

dailyGuidance.title: Rest in the nearness already given
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the tired mind that keeps searching elsewhere for relief. The line says intimacy arrives by grace, and then the running starts to lose its point.

dailyGuidance.title: Let nearness end the split vision
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the tired split between holy places and ordinary places. By grace, the Lord comes near enough for the chase to end: wherever you look, He is there.

dailyGuidance.title: Spend the remaining day on what lasts
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the life acting as if time were still abundant. The line says the day is shrinking, so use it for the profit of Naam now.

dailyGuidance.title: Bring the shrinking day to the Guru
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the day already passing while the important thing is still delayed. The line puts urgency beside hope: the Guru can still settle what matters.

dailyGuidance.title: Run to sanctuary before fear hardens
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the moment when the inner thieves are already upon you and composure is gone. The line does not pretend strength; it cries to the Father and takes shelter.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop exhausting yourself before prayer
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the worn-out mind still testing one more solution. The line turns fatigue into an honest cry to the Father.

dailyGuidance.title: Stand where fear cannot rule
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind starting to organize itself around threat instead of truth. The line calls for shelter before fear becomes the only voice in the room.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Guru's word rein the mind
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the unruly moment when cleverness wants dignity without being governed. The line says the mind is honored only when the Guru's word takes the reins.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Guru's goad train the wild mind
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the unruled mind while inner thieves keep stealing from it. The line says the Guru's mark gives direction, dignity, and a way to guard the treasure within.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the split mind surrender
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind being dragged by duality and bad counsel. The line says surrender through the Guru turns that divided mind back toward oneness.

dailyGuidance.title: Name the house duality built
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the mind that still thinks divided loyalties are harmless. The line treats duality as architecture you can quietly start living inside.

dailyGuidance.title: Ego cannot deliver the peace it promises
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self-willed life that still expects peace as a reward. The line says ego cannot make peace; it only keeps forgetting Naam.

dailyGuidance.title: Duality ruins what ego keeps defending
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the self asking for peace while clinging to divided loyalties. The line says unrest is not accidental; ego and duality keep feeding it.

dailyGuidance.title: Serve with one gathered awareness
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the split between outward service and an inwardly scattered mind. The line says service becomes true when awareness and love are gathered toward the One, and the self grows low enough to mean it.

dailyGuidance.title: Stop borrowing greatness from the world
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the reflex to stand near power and hope it will steady you. The line says the world's important people cannot save you; humble company can.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Guru's way outrank the powerful
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart still impressed by rank, influence, and size. The line says knowing the Guru's way outweighs millions of rewards.

dailyGuidance.title: Seek the humble servant, not the impressive name
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the heart still impressed by size, rank, and visible importance. The line says help is found with the humble servant, not with the world's celebrated names.

dailyGuidance.title: Guard one real instant of remembrance
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the scattered life excusing its drift. The line says a single instant of true remembrance outweighs a long distracted stretch.

dailyGuidance.title: One remembered instant outweighs filth
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets the shame that discounts a brief sincere return. The line gives one instant of remembrance real weight against a dirty habit.

dailyGuidance.title: Let the Guru's word lift you into real stature
dailyGuidance.summary: This meets ambition disguised as spiritual progress. The line says true stature is attained through the Guru's word, which steadies the mind from within.

shabadDeepDives.title: Hukam is the atmosphere of everything
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Japji Sahib, Pauri 2
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by placing form, life, greatness, pain, blessing, and wandering inside Hukam. It keeps widening that field until nothing stands outside the Command and ego has nowhere left to boast.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who is still dividing life into acceptable turns and unacceptable ones. Stayed with, it enlarges reality beyond protest and makes humility possible inside every condition.

shabadDeepDives.title: Wear contentment before you speak of conquest
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Japji Sahib, Pauri 28
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by taking visible yogic marks and turning them inward: contentment, humility, meditation, remembrance. It opens into brotherhood and comes to rest where true conquest happens, in the mind rather than the room.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels tempted by spiritual image, intensity, or performance. Taken seriously, it redirects discipline away from display and into a life that is humbler, steadier, and harder to fake.

shabadDeepDives.title: Human birth is a chance, not an ornament
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: So Purakh
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad refuses to flatter human life; it names it as a rare opening to meet the Lord while breath is still here. It moves from opportunity to urgency, pressing the hearer toward Naam, sangat, and a life that answers the chance it was given.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person busy enough to forget that life is more than maintenance and self-arrangement. Kept near, it turns a precious life from drift into response.

shabadDeepDives.title: Service without reward reaches the Master
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Gauree
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by defining the servant who lives in the Guru's household: obedient, unadvertised, and absorbed in Naam. It comes to a sharp center where selfless service without reward reaches the Lord Himself.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person doing good while keeping one eye on recognition. Lived with faithfully, it purifies service by taking self-display and reward out of the center.

shabadDeepDives.title: Ego is a chronic illness with a cure inside it
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Aasaa
shabadDeepDives.summary: Guru Angad does not flatter ego or mystify it. He names it as the pattern behind action and bondage, then says the cure appears through grace and the Guru's Shabad.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person who keeps locating every problem outside the self while anger, injury, and self-importance keep returning. Stay close to this shabad after conflict, and it turns self-diagnosis from shame into treatment.

shabadDeepDives.title: Pain tells the truth comfort hides
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Aasaa
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by reversing ordinary judgment: suffering can be medicine, while pleasure can become disease when it dulls desire for God. It then yields agency back to the Creator and widens into praise of the One whose light fills everything.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels clinging to comfort, resenting pain, or numbing every discomfort on contact. Held wisely, it changes pain from meaningless interruption into an unwanted but revealing teacher.

shabadDeepDives.title: Why waver under a merciful Creator
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Tilang
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by naming the Lord's mercy twice and grounding life in His gifts. It then asks why the mortal wavers when the One who created also nourishes, protects, and cherishes every heart.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels spiraling over provision, safety, or the future. Taken steadily, it pulls the mind back under mercy and teaches trust while breath remains.

shabadDeepDives.title: Mercy remembered becomes living Naam
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Mundhaavanee Fifth Mehl
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens in confession: I did not recognize what You did for me. It moves through unworthiness and pity received, then blooms when the True Guru is met and Naam makes body and mind green again.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person who has gone numb to mercy or embarrassed by their own ingratitude. Stayed with honestly, it turns shame into gratitude and gratitude into renewed life in Naam.

shabadDeepDives.title: Longing is led home in saintly company
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Maajh
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens in aching longing for the Beloved and admits it cannot find the way alone. It searches mind and body, turns toward saintly company, and keeps asking to be brought near.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person who feels alone, spiritually lost, or emotionally closed in. Taken faithfully, it changes loneliness from sealed isolation into guided longing and gives yearning somewhere truthful to go.

shabadDeepDives.title: Remembrance settles the body
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Gauree
shabadDeepDives.summary: The piece opens with remembrance repeated until peace reaches the body and anguish begins to loosen. It broadens into praise of the One Word behind scripture and ends by longing for the company of those who truly yearn for Darshan.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone whose worry has moved into the chest, gut, and shoulders. Kept near, it gives simran a bodily honesty instead of leaving it as decorative language.

shabadDeepDives.title: Honor the one through whom life arrives
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Aasaa
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by tracing birth, friendship, marriage, and lineage through woman. It then asks how she can be called bad when kings themselves are born from her, and ends in radiant mouths that praise the Lord.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels shaped by casual contempt, inherited patriarchy, or speech that lowers women while depending on them. Taken seriously, it restores reverence, humility, and a truer social imagination.

shabadDeepDives.title: The path is known by labor and generosity
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Saarang
shabadDeepDives.summary: The piece opens by exposing religious pose without wisdom, labor, or integrity behind it. It comes to a clean test: the one who works for what they eat and gives some away is the one who knows the path.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person confused by spiritual branding, costume, or authority language. Stayed with honestly, it returns discernment to labor, generosity, and humility.

shabadDeepDives.title: Rest where praise and possession lose their force
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Gauree
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by locating rest in the Lord's sanctuary. It then equalizes pleasure and pain, gold and copper, praise and slander, until attachment loses the right to name reality.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person whipped around by approval, possession, or comparison. Kept near, it makes detachment feel less like numbness and more like shelter strong enough to keep the heart even.

shabadDeepDives.title: Receiving under Hukam
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: So Purakh · Ang 11
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by placing all becoming, giving, and receiving in the Lord's pleasure. It opens further through separation and reunion, play and service, and ends where the Creator alone is doing all that happens.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person fighting outcomes they did not choose or trying to carry reality by force. Taken steadily, it teaches a cleaner receiving under Hukam and loosens the fist of resistance.

shabadDeepDives.title: Do not let speech carry filth
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 15
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by describing greed, falsehood, slander, and anger as degrading forms of speech and appetite. It then asks a harder question: what words actually bring honor at the Lord's Door?
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose hurt, sharpness, or cleverness keeps leaking out through the mouth. Stayed with honestly, it makes speech answerable to honor, not impulse.

shabadDeepDives.title: Doubt does not die by wandering
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 22
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by saying the fire of doubt is not quenched by roaming. It turns the mind toward the Guru's word, saintly company, and the surrender of selfishness until peace merges like water in water.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person who keeps moving, researching, and second-guessing without getting clearer. Taken seriously, it gives doubt a real treatment: the line is kept, ego loosens, and peace becomes more than an idea.

shabadDeepDives.title: Trade for what can follow you
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 22
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins with market language and turns it against ordinary appetite: buy what can go with you. It measures profit by praise, truth, and the wealth the Divine Merchant will still receive.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels trying to feel safe through buying, upgrading, or being seen as successful. Bring this shabad to the checkout screen, with the card in your hand, or before the monthly budget meeting, and let it ask the question appetite avoids: what here can still follow you?

shabadDeepDives.title: Peace shows up in speech and gait
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 31
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens by exposing ritual performed from self-will as the misery of an unwanted bride. It directs the heart toward saintly company and one-pointed Naam, then shows the fruit plainly: sweet speech, humble walking, and peace within.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose devotional language still outruns their conduct. Kept close, it lets peace become visible in tone, pace, and the body's way of moving through the world.

shabadDeepDives.title: Roaming ends where holy company cools the heart
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Maajh · Ang 98
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens in relentless searching through forests, philosophies, rituals, and yogic techniques. It turns only when mercy brings true company, and then the mind and body finally cool.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person trapped in spiritual roaming, method-switching, and never-arriving effort. Taken seriously, it says peace is not found by multiplying techniques but by mercy and true company.

shabadDeepDives.title: Forgiveness is the fast that makes one fearless
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 223
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by naming forgiveness, good conduct, and contentment as the real fast. It travels through release from disease and death-fear and comes to rest in the Lord already present within and without.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person holding hurt so tightly that it has started feeling like identity. Taken faithfully, it turns forgiveness from sentiment into discipline and lets fear lose some of its hidden power.

shabadDeepDives.title: True bankers trade in Naam
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 257
shabadDeepDives.summary: The pauree opens by saying the mind's wandering stops in the company of saints. It then names the true bankers as those whose wealth is the Name and whose patience, honor, and glory ripen from listening well.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels chasing quick gains, visible results, or restless proof. Stayed with consistently, it redefines wealth, slows the heart, and lets patience become a real form of honor.

shabadDeepDives.title: Religion measured by Naam and conduct
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 266
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens by ranking the path plainly: the best religion is Naam joined to pure conduct. It moves through cleansing the dirty mind in holy company and ends with the Lord's Name kept living in the heart.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose language of devotion has started outrunning the life carrying it. Stayed with honestly, it closes the split between speech and conduct and makes remembrance answerable to daily behavior.

shabadDeepDives.title: The humble are kept close
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Raamkalee · Ang 882
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens with the Guru as great giver, planting the Lord within the heart. It carries the listener through hearing the Guru's teaching, exposing lesser cravings, and ends with the Lord holding His humble servant close like a cherished child.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose sense of worth keeps depending on attention, beauty, or riches. Stayed with gently, it turns worth into something received from being held near the Lord.

shabadDeepDives.title: Forgiveness settles into lasting peace
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Raag Sorath · Ang 628
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins with the Perfect Guru's completed work: forgiveness given, peace found. It opens wider into peace spreading everywhere and comes to rest in singing the Guru's Bani and meditating on Naam.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person who has tasted relief but does not yet know how to live from it. Stayed with, it keeps peace from becoming a passing feeling and turns it into praise, devotion, and a different atmosphere.

shabadDeepDives.title: Truth before beginning, truth through time
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Jap · Ang 1
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens by naming Truth before time, mood, or human history. It strips away silence, accumulation, and cleverness, before coming to rest in the question of how falsehood breaks: by walking in Hukam.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person swollen with urgency, cleverness, or spiritual self-effort. Kept close, it changes scale: your fear stops posing as ultimate, and you begin learning how to live under what is already true.

shabadDeepDives.title: Praise breaks the illusion of mastery
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Jap · Ang 1
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins with many voices singing different dimensions of the Lord's power, gifts, beauty, knowledge, making, and unmaking. It opens the field so wide that control, ownership, and single-angle thinking start to look small.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels gripping reality too tightly and mistaking analysis for authority. Stayed with honestly, it restores scale and invites praise where the mind wanted to dominate.

shabadDeepDives.title: Remember together, not in isolation
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 17
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by calling spiritual companions close and asking them to speak of the Lord together. It carries the listener through humility, sweet speech, and the Guru's Shabad, then ends with the True King drawing the heart into Himself.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose remembrance has gone flat in private heaviness. Held warmly, it turns companionship into a place where gratitude, virtue, and shared remembrance can breathe again.

shabadDeepDives.title: Fear leaves when schemes do
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 18
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens with rescue arriving alongside subdued ego. It travels through useless plans being abandoned, fear leaving by meeting the True One, and ends in the genuine merchandise recognized through the Guru.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person trying to survive by cleverness, image-management, or endless contingency planning. Taken seriously, it turns salvation away from schemes and back toward the Guru's truth.

shabadDeepDives.title: Praise melts what comparison hardens
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 18
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens with metal merging into metal and uses that image to describe praise absorbed into the Praiseworthy Lord. It carries the listener through saintly dust, true action, and the home of the self being found within.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone whose mind keeps hardening around comparison, self-consciousness, or restless ambition. Kept near, it softens the separate self and turns it toward praise, holy company, and homecoming.

shabadDeepDives.title: Duality makes decoration hollow
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 18
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by calling the life deceived by duality cursed and unstable like a wall of sand. It travels through the uselessness of decoration without the Beloved and ends where beauty becomes real only by being pierced with the Shabad.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person still trying to fix inner separation with outer polish. Stayed with honestly, it exposes display without love and turns the heart back toward the Beloved.

shabadDeepDives.title: Ask the Guru before you multiply the questions
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 34
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens with an exposed question: whom shall I serve, what shall I chant? It answers by accepting the True Guru's will, uprooting selfishness, and letting Naam bring peace into the mind.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels exhausted by indecision, self-invention, or spiritual sampling. Stayed with honestly, it changes the search itself: the question becomes cleaner, the ego quieter, and practice less scattered.

shabadDeepDives.title: Do not postpone remembrance
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 35
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by exposing the delaying mind that keeps waiting for the right time to remember the Lord. It responds with day-and-night attunement and devotion that does not forget the Beloved even briefly.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person who respects practice in principle but keeps scheduling it out of reach. Taken steadily, it breaks procrastination's spell and teaches constancy more than intensity.

shabadDeepDives.title: The Shabad clears the double mind
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 35
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens with contemplation of the Guru's word and the reverence it produces. It moves into abiding in true company, casting off duality, and ending in speech and mind made truthful by love.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who keeps reopening certainty until it turns cloudy. Taken faithfully, it gives doubt a cleaner answer than endless thought: remain with the Shabad until the split mind thins.

shabadDeepDives.title: Mercy lets the child tell the truth
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 51
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens in tenderness and dependence: the soul leans on the Lord's mercy and admits its mistakes as a child would. It then confesses how hard Hukam is to accept and ends in recognition of the Supreme Lord through the Guru.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone who feels stuck between shame and self-protection after failure. Stayed with sincerely, it makes confession safer and trust more childlike.

shabadDeepDives.title: Humble company ends the fight underneath the fight
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 52
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by saying that meeting the humble defeats the messenger of death. It pushes deeper through the Lord dwelling in the mind, worldly entanglements ending, and the Guru's grace becoming ambrosial Naam.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person whose heat, fear, or defensiveness keeps masquerading as strength. Keep this shabad close when you want to fight alone, and it will remind you that the company you enter is already shaping your courage.

shabadDeepDives.title: Love the Guru with mind and body
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 52
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by fastening mind and body to the Guru in love. It broadens through obedience, Sangat, and the dust-like poverty of Maya-attachment, then ends in total remembrance: this life, body, and breath are Yours.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person whose love has been scattered across comforts, approval, and restless seeking. Kept close, it gathers desire back to one center and turns company, conduct, and remembrance into a single path.

shabadDeepDives.title: Release arrives where seeking kneels into service
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 52
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad begins by declaring that release comes only through the True Name. It turns seeking toward the Guru's feet, true service, and the hidden Lord found when the True Guru is pleased.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person who keeps searching but cannot land. Taken steadily, it ends the addiction to spiritual novelty and teaches that arrival comes through service, not endless roaming.

shabadDeepDives.title: Fresh Naam enters the mind
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 69
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens by promising freedom from the old cycle through meeting the True Guru. It moves through understanding given by the Shabad and rests in the ever-fresh Naam abiding within the mind.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person worn out by inner repetition and hungry for something truly renewing. Return to this shabad before reaching for novelty, and it will move refreshment from outside stimulation to Naam settling within.

shabadDeepDives.title: Truth is meant to occupy the whole life
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 69
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by joining service to the True Guru with the cleansing of mind and body. Then it keeps widening truth until it touches food, speech, company, clothing, and shelter.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This is for anyone whose devotion still lives in a separate room from the rest of the day. Stay with it when prayer and conduct drift apart; it insists that truth should enter the whole way you live.

shabadDeepDives.title: Peace comes through serving the True Guru
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 85
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad starts by joining service, peace, and the treasure of the True Name. It deepens through self-recognition, inner light, truthfulness, and praise that returns body and soul to the Lord.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This one meets the person wanting peace without surrendering the center seat. Reach for it before self-justification or image-management takes over, and it will press peace back through service, recognition, and praise.

shabadDeepDives.title: All belong to the One who belongs to all
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
shabadDeepDives.summary: The shabad opens by overturning private ownership: all are Yours, and You belong to all. It broadens into dependence, prayer, nearness, and the recognition that without the Lord there is not even a place to stand.
shabadDeepDives.whyItMatters: This speaks to the person shrinking worth into possession, status, or exclusivity. Kept close, it changes the emotional climate from scarcity to shared dependence and from ego to belonging.

shabadDeepDives.title: Learning without inward turning stays trapped in Maya
shabadDeepDives.subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
